_comment: Golden evaluation set for RAG pipeline. Each entry has: id, query, expected_facts (claims the answer MUST contain), expected_chunks (text substrings that should appear in accepted_chunks), category, difficulty. expected_chunk_ids are doc_id:chunk_index pairs — leave empty to rely on text-substring matching only.

cases.query: What BLEU score did the Transformer achieve on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task?
expected_facts: The Transformer (big) achieved 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German
This improved over existing best results including ensembles by over 2 BLEU

cases.query: How many attention heads does the Transformer base model use?
expected_facts: The Transformer base model uses 8 parallel attention heads

cases.query: What is the dimensionality of the model (dmodel) in the Transformer base model?
expected_facts: The dimensionality dmodel is 512 in the base Transformer model

cases.query: What optimizer was used to train the Transformer?
expected_facts: The Adam optimizer was used
Beta1 was 0.9 and beta2 was 0.98

cases.query: What types of regularization were used during Transformer training?
expected_facts: Residual dropout was applied to the output of each sub-layer
Label smoothing of value 0.1 was employed during training

cases.query: How does the Transformer's positional encoding work?
expected_facts: Positional encodings use sine and cosine functions of different frequencies
The wavelengths form a geometric progression from 2 pi to 10000 times 2 pi

cases.query: What is Scaled Dot-Product Attention and how is it computed?
expected_facts: Queries and keys have dimension dk and values have dimension dv
The dot products of queries with keys are divided by the square root of dk
A softmax function is applied to obtain the weights on the values

cases.query: How long did it take to train the Transformer big model?
expected_facts: The big model was trained for 3.5 days
Training was done on 8 P100 GPUs

cases.query: What BLEU score did the Transformer achieve on the English-to-French translation task?
expected_facts: The Transformer achieved a BLEU score of 41.8 on WMT 2014 English-to-French
This was a new single-model state-of-the-art

cases.query: What is Multi-Head Attention and why is it used instead of single-head attention?
expected_facts: Multi-head attention linearly projects queries keys and values h times with different learned projections
It allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces
With a single attention head averaging inhibits attending to different subspaces

cases.query: How does the Transformer compare to recurrent models in terms of computational complexity?
expected_facts: Self-attention layers connect all positions with a constant number of sequentially executed operations
A recurrent layer requires O(n) sequential operations
Self-attention layers are faster than recurrent layers when sequence length is smaller than representation dimensionality

cases.query: What is the encoder structure in the Transformer?
expected_chunks_text: encoder is composed of a stack of N = 6
expected_facts: The encoder is composed of a stack of N equals 6 identical layers
Each layer has two sub-layers: multi-head self-attention and a position-wise feed-forward network
Residual connections are employed around each sub-layer followed by layer normalization

cases.query: What training data was used for the English-German translation task?
expected_facts: The standard WMT 2014 English-German dataset was used
It consists of about 4.5 million sentence pairs
Sentences were encoded using byte-pair encoding with about 37000 tokens

cases.query: What is the feed-forward network structure in the Transformer?
expected_facts: Each layer contains a fully connected feed-forward network applied to each position separately
It consists of two linear transformations with a ReLU activation in between
The inner-layer has dimensionality dff equals 2048

cases.query: How did the Transformer perform on English constituency parsing?
expected_facts: The Transformer performed well on English constituency parsing
It achieved 91.3 F1 in the WSJ-only discriminative setting
In the semi-supervised setting it achieved 92.7 F1

cases.query: Why does dot-product attention use a scaling factor?
expected_facts: For large values of dk the dot products grow large in magnitude
This pushes the softmax function into regions where it has extremely small gradients
The dot products are scaled by 1 over the square root of dk to counteract this effect

cases.query: What are the three ways multi-head attention is used in the Transformer?
expected_facts: In encoder-decoder attention layers queries come from the previous decoder layer and keys and values come from the encoder output
The encoder contains self-attention layers where all keys values and queries come from the output of the previous encoder layer
Self-attention layers in the decoder allow each position to attend to all positions up to and including that position

cases.query: Summarize the main contribution of the Attention Is All You Need paper
expected_facts: The paper proposes the Transformer architecture based solely on attention mechanisms
It dispenses with recurrence and convolutions entirely
The model achieves state-of-the-art results on machine translation tasks while being more parallelizable

cases.query: What warmup schedule was used for the learning rate during Transformer training?
expected_facts: The learning rate was increased linearly for the first warmup_steps training steps
After warmup it decreased proportionally to the inverse square root of the step number
warmup_steps was set to 4000

cases.query: What dropout rate was used in the Transformer base model?
expected_facts: The base model used a dropout rate of 0.1

cases.query: What is the Singleton design pattern?
expected_facts: Singleton ensures a class has only one instance
It provides a global point of access to that instance

cases.query: What is the Factory Method pattern and give a real-world example?
expected_facts: Factory Method defines an interface for creating an object but lets subclasses decide which class to instantiate
A logistics company is given as an example where createTransport factory method lets each subclass decide what vehicle to create

cases.query: What is the Abstract Factory pattern?
expected_facts: Abstract Factory provides an interface for creating families of related or dependent objects without specifying their concrete classes

cases.query: What are the three categories of design patterns according to the Gang of Four?
expected_facts: Design patterns are grouped into three categories: Creational, Structural, and Behavioral
They were popularized by the Gang of Four in their 1994 book

cases.query: What is a real-world example of the Singleton pattern?
expected_facts: A configuration manager in an application is a real-world example of the Singleton pattern
The app should read the config file once and reuse that single instance everywhere

cases.query: Compare the Transformer's approach to sequence modeling with traditional RNN approaches
expected_facts: Recurrent models generate hidden states sequentially which precludes parallelization
The Transformer relies entirely on attention mechanisms instead of recurrence
The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization

cases.query: What advantages does self-attention have over convolutional layers for sequence transduction?
expected_facts: Self-attention connects all positions with a constant number of operations
Convolutional layers require a stack of O(n/k) layers to connect all pairs of positions
Self-attention could yield more interpretable models

cases.query: How many layers does the decoder have in the Transformer base model?
expected_chunks_text: decoder is also composed of a stack of N = 6
expected_facts: The decoder is composed of a stack of N equals 6 identical layers
The decoder inserts a third sub-layer which performs multi-head attention over the encoder output

cases.query: What hardware was used to train the Transformer base model and how long did it take?
expected_facts: Training was done on one machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs
The base model was trained for 100000 steps or 12 hours
Each training step took about 0.4 seconds for the base model

cases.query: How does label smoothing affect the Transformer's performance?
expected_facts: Label smoothing of value 0.1 was used
It hurts perplexity as the model learns to be more unsure
But it improves accuracy and BLEU score

cases.query: What is the role of masking in the decoder self-attention?
expected_chunks_text: prevent positions from attending to subsequent positions
expected_facts: The self-attention sub-layer in the decoder is modified to prevent positions from attending to subsequent positions
This masking combined with output embeddings being offset by one position ensures predictions for position i depend only on known outputs at positions less than i

cases.query: What problem do creational design patterns solve?
expected_facts: Creational patterns deal with object creation mechanisms
They aim to create objects in a manner suitable to the situation

cases.query: How does the embedding weight sharing work in the Transformer?
expected_facts: The same weight matrix is shared between the two embedding layers and the pre-softmax linear transformation
In the embedding layers those weights are multiplied by the square root of dmodel

cases.query: What beam search parameters were used during Transformer inference?
expected_facts: Beam search was used with a beam size of 4
A length penalty alpha of 0.6 was used
Maximum output length was set to input length plus 50

cases.query: What previous models did the Transformer outperform on English-to-German translation?
expected_facts: The Transformer outperformed ByteNet, GNMT with RL, ConvS2S, and MoE models
It outperformed even the best ensemble models
